Beaumont Hamel British Cemetery is a World War I military cemetery located near Beaumont Hamel in the Somme region of northern France. It is associated with the Battle of the Somme, one of the largest and bloodiest battles of World War I. Here are some key details:

1. Location: The cemetery is situated in the Picardy region of France, close to the site of significant fighting during the Battle of the Somme in 1916.

2. Historical Significance: It commemorates British soldiers who were killed during the Battle of the Somme, particularly during the first day of the battle on July 1, 1916, which was one of the deadliest days in British military history.

3. Design: Like many Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemeteries, it is carefully maintained with rows of white headstones and well-kept grounds.

4. Burials: The cemetery contains the graves of soldiers who died during the battles in this area, primarily British soldiers from World War I.

5. Memorial: It serves as a place of remembrance and commemoration for those who lost their lives during the conflict.
